indication.text: ANKTIVA in combination with BCG is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors.

citations.quote: ANKTIVA in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors.

target_moa.text: Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln is an IL-15 receptor agonist; given as a boost to the trained immunity induced by BCG (prime), it generates memory T cells and memory NK cells with enhanced efficacy and durable response.

citations.quote: Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmnl (N-803, ALT-803, Anktiva) is an IL-15 receptor agonist for the proposed indication and usage with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) for the treatment of patients with BCG-unresponsive nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors.

The synergistic immunological activity of N-803 (as a boost) to the trained immunity induced by BCG (prime), results in the generation of memory T cells and memory NK cells with enhanced efficacy and a durable response rate in patients with BCG-unresponsive bladder cancer.

modality.text: Other – recombinant fusion protein complex (IL-15 superagonist): nogapendekin alfa (IL-15N72D variant) bound to inbakicept (IL-15Rα sushi domain/IgG1 Fc fusion protein).

citations.quote: Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmnl is a soluble complex consisting of (a) nogapendekin alfa (a human IL-15N72D variant, 114 amino acids) bound to (b) inbakicept [a dimeric human IL-15R\alpha sushi domain (65 amino acids)/human IgG1 Fc fusion protein (232 amino acids)].

key_safety.text: Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions were increased creatinine, dysuria (32%), hematuria (32%), urinary frequency (27%), micturition urgency (25%), urinary tract infection (24%), increased potassium, musculoskeletal pain (17%), chills (15%) and pyrexia (15%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 16% of patients; a fatal cardiac arrest occurred in 1 (1.1%) patient.
